subproblem.title: Fubini on the product plane π⁻¹(span τ) for compactly supported continuous f
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k], Φ(s, u) := (s, u_1, …, u_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ u))), π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^P (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))), and assume (MP): for every A ⊆ ℝ^P that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A), where Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2) on ℝ × ℝ^P and L¹ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (τ : Fin m → ℝ^P), T := span ℝ (range τ), and let f : ℝ^{P+1} → ℝ be continuous with compact support. Then ∫_{{z : π(z) ∈ T}} f dH^{m+1} = ∫_ℝ (∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w)) dσ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3(b) and Step 15 of the parent proof ((MP) applies to the plane T = span τ; change of variables along Φ′ and Fubini for the compactly supported continuous integrand f∘Φ′).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := volume on ℝ. Φ(s, u) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ u)); π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y)); y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0; Φ′ : ℝ × E → E′, Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2). (MP) is the hypothesis: for every A ⊆ E that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A). T := span ℝ (range τ).

1. (Φ′ is a homeomorphism.) Φ′ is continuous: p ↦ Fin.cons p.1 (EuclideanSpace.equiv p.2) is continuous (Continuous.finCons with continuous_fst and the continuous equivalence composed with continuous_snd), and so is the inverse equivalence. The map y ↦ (y₀, π(y)) is continuous (coordinate projections, continuous_pi, continuous_apply). They are mutually inverse: (Φ(s, u)₀, π(Φ(s, u))) = (s, u) by Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons and ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply/symm_apply_apply; and Φ(y₀, π(y)) = y because both sides have the same image under the injective EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin.cons_self_tail). Hence Φ′ underlies a homeomorphism e : ℝ × E ≃ₜ E′, and Φ′ is a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).
2. (dim T = m.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so finrank ℝ T = card (Fin m) = m (finrank_span_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin).
3. (T is null-measurable.) T is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), hence Borel measurable, hence Hᵐ-null-measurable.
4. (T is countably m-rectifiable.) Let Λₗ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) →ₗ E be Λₗ(u) := Σ_i u_i·τ_i (Fintype.linearCombination ℝ τ composed with EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ). Its domain is finite-dimensional, so Λₗ is a continuous linear map Λ (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap), and Λ is Lipschitz (ContinuousLinearMap.lipschitzWith). range Λ = T: if v = Λ(u) then v = Σ_i u_i τ_i ∈ T; conversely, if v ∈ T then v = Σ_i c_i τ_i for some c : Fin m → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun) and v = Λ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm c). Hence T = range Λ is countably m-rectifiable (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_range).
5. (T is locally Hᵐ-finite.) Since finrank T = m (step 2), the measure Hᵐ⌞T is regular (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), in particular finite on compact sets. For compact K (closed, hence Borel), Hᵐ(T ∩ K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ T) = (Hᵐ⌞T)(K) < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply, IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Also Hᵐ⌞T is σ-finite (finite on compacts in the σ-compact space E).
6. (Apply (MP).) Steps 3–5 verify the three hypotheses of (MP) for A = T, so H^{m+1}⌞{z : π(z) ∈ T} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T).
7. (Change of variables.) ∫_{{z : π(z) ∈ T}} f dH^{m+1} = ∫ f d(H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ T}) = ∫ f d(Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T)) (step 6) = ∫ f∘Φ′ d(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, step 1; valid for every integrand).
8. (Integrability.) f∘Φ′ = f∘e is continuous and has compact support, because e is a homeomorphism and f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). L¹ and Hᵐ⌞T are finite on compact sets and σ-finite, so their product is finite on compact sets (instance Measure.prod.instIsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). A continuous function with compact support is integrable for a measure that is finite on compact sets (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). Hence f∘Φ′ is (L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T)-integrable.
9. (Fubini.) By integral_prod (step 8; Hᵐ⌞T s-finite), ∫ f∘Φ′ d(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞T) = ∫_ℝ (∫ f(Φ(σ, w)) d(Hᵐ⌞T)(w)) dσ = ∫_ℝ (∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w)) dσ.
10. (Conclusion.) Steps 7 and 9 give ∫_{{z : π(z) ∈ T}} f dH^{m+1} = ∫_ℝ ∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dHᵐ(w) dσ. ∎

Source: Steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof (orthonormality of τ̃ = (e₀, ιτ), dim Q = m + 1, and Q = π⁻¹(T) as sets), with the coordinate facts (F1)–(F3).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1). Φ(s, u) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ u)) = (s, u_1, …, u_P); π(z) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ z)) = (z_1, …, z_P); z₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ z) 0; e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1; τ̃ := Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => Φ(0, τ_i)) : Fin (m+1) → E′, so τ̃_0 = e₀ and τ̃_{i+1} = Φ(0, τ_i) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ); T := span ℝ (range τ); Q := span ℝ (range τ̃).

1. (Coordinates.) The coordinates of Φ(s, u) are Φ(s, u)₀ = s and Φ(s, u)_{j+1} = u_j (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ). Hence π(Φ(s, u)) = u (Fin.tail_cons, ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply). Moreover every z ∈ E′ satisfies z = Φ(z₀, π(z)): both sides have the same image under the injective map EuclideanSpace.equiv, because Fin.cons (q 0) (Fin.tail q) = q (Fin.cons_self_tail).
2. (e₀ = Φ(1, 0).) Compare coordinates by Fin.cases: at index 0 both equal 1; at index j+1, e₀ has coordinate 0 (j+1 ≠ 0, Fin.succ_ne_zero) and Φ(1, 0) has coordinate 0. Hence τ̃_0 = Φ(1, 0).
3. (Inner products.) For a, b ∈ ℝ and u, w ∈ E: ⟨Φ(a, u), Φ(b, w)⟩ = Σ_{i : Fin (P+1)} Φ(a, u)_i·Φ(b, w)_i (PiLp.inner_apply) = a·b + Σ_{j : Fin P} u_j·w_j (Fin.sum_univ_succ and step 1) = a·b + ⟨u, w⟩.
4. (τ̃ is orthonormal.) By orthonormal_iff_ite it suffices to show ⟨τ̃_i, τ̃_j⟩ = (1 if i = j else 0) for all i, j : Fin (m+1). Split i and j with Fin.cases and use steps 2, 3:
   - i = j = 0: ⟨Φ(1,0), Φ(1,0)⟩ = 1·1 + ⟨0, 0⟩ = 1.
   - i = 0, j = j′+1: ⟨Φ(1,0), Φ(0,τ_{j′})⟩ = 1·0 + ⟨0, τ_{j′}⟩ = 0, and 0 ≠ j′+1.
   - i = i′+1, j = 0: symmetric, value 0, and i′+1 ≠ 0.
   - i = i′+1, j = j′+1: ⟨Φ(0,τ_{i′}), Φ(0,τ_{j′})⟩ = 0 + ⟨τ_{i′}, τ_{j′}⟩ = (1 if i′ = j′ else 0) because τ is orthonormal, and i′+1 = j′+1 iff i′ = j′ (Fin.succ_inj).
5. (finrank Q = m + 1.) An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so finrank ℝ Q = card (Fin (m+1)) = m + 1 (finrank_span_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin).
6. (π is linear.) Fin.tail q = q ∘ Fin.succ, so π is the composite linear map πₗ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm ∘ₗ LinearMap.funLeft ℝ ℝ Fin.succ ∘ₗ (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ), and πₗ z = π(z) holds by definition (rfl). Let Z := T.comap πₗ, a submodule of E′ whose underlying set is {z : π(z) ∈ T}.
7. (Φ is linear.) For a, b, c ∈ ℝ and u, w ∈ E: Φ(a, u) + Φ(b, w) = Φ(a + b, u + w) and c·Φ(a, u) = Φ(c·a, c·u) (pull the sum/scalar inside the linear equivalences with map_add/map_smul and compare coordinates by Fin.cases), and Φ(0, 0) = 0. By induction over finite sets (Finset.induction_on), Σ_{i∈s} Φ(a_i, u_i) = Φ(Σ_{i∈s} a_i, Σ_{i∈s} u_i).
8. (Q ≤ Z.) By Submodule.span_le it suffices that every τ̃_i lies in Z. By Fin.cases: π(τ̃_0) = π(Φ(1, 0)) = 0 ∈ T (zero_mem), and π(τ̃_{i+1}) = π(Φ(0, τ_i)) = τ_i ∈ T (Submodule.subset_span), using step 1.
9. (Z ≤ Q.) Let z ∈ Z, i.e. π(z) ∈ T. By Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun there is c : Fin m → ℝ with Σ_i c_i·τ_i = π(z). By steps 2 and 7, z₀·τ̃_0 + Σ_i c_i·τ̃_{i+1} = Φ(z₀·1, z₀·0) + Σ_i Φ(c_i·0, c_i·τ_i) = Φ(z₀, Σ_i c_i·τ_i) = Φ(z₀, π(z)) = z (step 1). Each summand lies in Q (subset_span, smul_mem, sum_mem, add_mem), hence z ∈ Q.
10. (Conclusion.) Steps 8 and 9 give Q = Z, hence (Q : Set E′) = (Z : Set E′) = {z : π(z) ∈ T}. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves all three claims. ∎

subproblem.title: Uniform mass bound for blow-ups at a point with a weighted approximate tangent plane
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵐ := μHE[m], M ⊆ ℝ^P Hᵐ-null-measurable, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ ≥ 0 on M and θ Hᵐ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K, x ∈ ℝ^P and T a linear subspace of ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M θ x T (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7). Then for every R ∈ ℝ there is B ∈ ℝ such that for all sufficiently small r > 0 (eventually in 𝓝[>] 0), every C ∈ ℝ and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ with |g(w)| ≤ C for all w and g(w) = 0 whenever ‖w‖ > R satisfy |∫_{η_r(M)} g(w)·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ(w)| ≤ C·B, where η_r := blowUpMap x r, η_r(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 12 of the parent proof (uniform domination of the blown-up slices via the cut-off g₀ and the tangent hypothesis applied to g₀), stated for an arbitrary integrand g bounded by C and vanishing outside B̄(0, R).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, Hᵐ := μHE[m], ν := Hᵐ⌞M. For r > 0, η_r := blowUpMap x r, η_r(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x). The sibling blowup_cov (the accepted declaration fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral) states: for every n, centre c, r > 0, set S and function h, ∫_{blowUpMap c r '' S} h dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹·∫_S h(blowUpMap c r z) dHⁿ(z), with no measurability or integrability assumption. The tangent hypothesis HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M θ x T says in particular (second component): for every φ ∈ C_c(E), ∫_{η_r(M)} φ(w)·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ(w) → θ(x)·∫_T φ dHᵐ as r → 0⁺.

1. (Cut-off.) Let g₀(w) := max(0, min(1, R + 1 − ‖w‖)). It is continuous (continuous_const.max, .min, .sub continuous_norm). It satisfies 0 ≤ g₀ ≤ 1; g₀(w) = 1 when ‖w‖ ≤ R (then R + 1 − ‖w‖ ≥ 1); and g₀(w) = 0 when ‖w‖ > R + 1 (then min(1, R + 1 − ‖w‖) < 0). So the support of g₀ lies in the compact ball B̄(0, R + 1) (HasCompactSupport.intro) and g₀ defines an element G₀ ∈ C_c(E) (CompactlySupportedContinuousMap built from g₀).
2. (Choice of B.) By the tangent hypothesis applied to G₀, b(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} g₀(w)·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ(w) tends to L₀ := θ(x)·∫_T g₀ dHᵐ as r → 0⁺. Put B := L₀ + 1 > L₀. Then eventually in 𝓝[>] 0 we have b(r) < B (Filter.Tendsto.eventually_lt_const), and eventually r > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Fix such an r, and fix C ∈ ℝ and g : E → ℝ with |g(w)| ≤ C for all w and g(w) = 0 whenever R < ‖w‖. It remains to show |∫_{η_r(M)} g(w)·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ(w)| ≤ C·B.
3. (θ is measurable and ν-a.e. nonnegative.) M = ⋃_{n∈ℕ} (M ∩ B̄(0, n)) (each u satisfies ‖u‖ ≤ ⌈‖u‖⌉₊). On each M ∩ B̄(0, n), θ is Hᵐ-integrable (the hypothesis on θ with the compact set K = B̄(0, n)), hence a.e. strongly measurable; so θ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). Since M is Hᵐ-null-measurable, ν-a.e. u lies in M (ae_restrict_mem₀), hence θ(u) ≥ 0 for ν-a.e. u.
4. (Undoing the blow-up.) For every h : E → ℝ, blowup_cov (n = m, centre x, set M, function w ↦ h(w)·θ(x + r·w), r > 0) gives ∫_{η_r(M)} h(w)·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ(w) = (r^m)⁻¹·∫_M h(η_r(u))·θ(x + r·η_r(u)) dHᵐ(u) = (r^m)⁻¹·∫_M h(η_r(u))·θ(u) dHᵐ(u), because x + r·(r⁻¹·(u − x)) = u (smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀, one_smul, add_sub_cancel).
5. (Integrability of u ↦ g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u) on M.) It is a.e. strongly measurable for ν (g₀∘η_r is continuous; times θ, step 3). ‖η_r(u)‖ = r⁻¹·‖u − x‖, so if u ∉ B̄(x, r(R+1)) then ‖η_r(u)‖ > R + 1 and g₀(η_r(u)) = 0. With 0 ≤ g₀ ≤ 1 this gives |g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u)| ≤ 1_{B̄(x, r(R+1))}(u)·|θ(u)| for every u. The right side is ν-integrable: by integrable_indicator_iff and Measure.restrict_restrict this is integrability of |θ| on M ∩ B̄(x, r(R+1)), which holds since this ball is compact. Hence u ↦ g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u) is ν-integrable (Integrable.mono').
6. (Pointwise comparison.) C ≥ 0, because 0 ≤ |g(0)| ≤ C. For every w, |g(w)| ≤ C·g₀(w): if ‖w‖ ≤ R then g₀(w) = 1 and |g(w)| ≤ C; otherwise g(w) = 0 and C·g₀(w) ≥ 0. Consequently, for ν-a.e. u (those with θ(u) ≥ 0), |g(η_r(u))·θ(u)| = |g(η_r(u))|·θ(u) ≤ C·g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u).
7. (Integral estimate.) |∫_M g(η_r(u))·θ(u) dHᵐ| ≤ ∫_M |g(η_r(u))·θ(u)| dHᵐ (norm_integral_le_integral_norm; no integrability needed) ≤ ∫_M C·g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u) dHᵐ (integral_mono_of_nonneg: the left integrand is nonnegative, the right one is ν-integrable by step 5, and step 6 gives the ν-a.e. inequality) = C·∫_M g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u) dHᵐ (integral_const_mul).
8. (Conclusion.) By step 4 with h = g and (r^m)⁻¹ > 0: |∫_{η_r(M)} g(w)·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ| = (r^m)⁻¹·|∫_M g(η_r(u))·θ(u) dHᵐ| ≤ (r^m)⁻¹·C·∫_M g₀(η_r(u))·θ(u) dHᵐ (step 7) = C·b(r) (step 4 with h = g₀) ≤ C·B (C ≥ 0 and b(r) < B). This holds for every r in the eventual set of step 2 and all C, g as stated. ∎

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3(a), 4 and 6–10 of the parent proof: undo both blow-ups with blowup_cov; blow-ups of the product are products of blow-ups; transport to the product measure (sibling product_measure); Fubini; substitution s = s₀ + rσ in the interval variable. The hypothesis s₀ ∈ (0,1) is not needed for this identity.

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := volume on ℝ. Φ(s, u) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ u)); π(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y)); y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0; Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2). M̃ := {y : π(y) ∈ M ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)}; y* := Φ(s₀, x); η := blowUpMap y* r on E′ and η′ := blowUpMap x r on E (η(z) = r⁻¹·(z − y*), η′(u) = r⁻¹·(u − x)), r > 0; ν := Hᵐ⌞M; ρ := (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν; a(σ) := ∫_{η′(M)} f(Φ(σ, w))·θ(x + r·w) dHᵐ(w); α := −s₀/r, β := (1 − s₀)/r. The goal is ∫_{η(M̃)} f(z)·θ(π(y* + r·z)) dH^{m+1}(z) = ∫_ℝ 1_{(α, β]}(σ)·a(σ) dσ.
Siblings used: blowup_cov (accepted declaration fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral): for every n, centre c, r > 0, set S and function h, ∫_{blowUpMap c r '' S} h dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹·∫_S h(blowUpMap c r z) dHⁿ(z), with no measurability or integrability assumption. product_measure (iwl_cr_ip_wt_product_measure): from (MP) and the hypotheses on M, H^{m+1}⌞M̃ = Φ′_*ρ.

1. (Coordinates.) π(Φ(s, u)) = u (ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, Fin.tail_cons, symm_apply_apply). Φ is linear in the pair: Φ(s, u) − Φ(s′, u′) = Φ(s − s′, u − u′) and c·Φ(s, u) = Φ(c·s, c·u) (map_sub/map_smul of the equivalences, coordinates compared by Fin.cases). ‖Φ(s, u)‖² = s² + ‖u‖² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, Fin.sum_univ_succ), so ‖u‖ ≤ ‖Φ(s, u)‖. Φ′ is continuous, with continuous inverse y ↦ (y₀, π(y)) (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail); so Φ′ is a homeomorphism ℝ × E ≃ₜ E′ and a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).
2. (Bounds on f.) Choose R with ‖z‖ ≤ R whenever f(z) ≠ 0 (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded), and C_f with |f(z)| ≤ C_f for all z (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). By step 1: (*) if f(Φ(σ, w)) ≠ 0 then ‖w‖ ≤ R.
3. (ν and θ.) ν is finite on compact sets: ν(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ M) = Hᵐ(M ∩ K) < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply). Hence ν is σ-finite (E is σ-compact). θ is a.e. strongly measurable for ν: M = ⋃_n (M ∩ B̄(0, n)), and θ is integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable, on each M ∩ B̄(0, n) (the hypothesis on θ with the compact set K = B̄(0, n)); conclude by aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff.
4. (Blow-ups.) For all s ∈ ℝ, u ∈ E: η(Φ(s, u)) = r⁻¹·(Φ(s, u) − Φ(s₀, x)) = Φ(r⁻¹·(s − s₀), r⁻¹·(u − x)) = Φ(r⁻¹·(s − s₀), η′(u)) (step 1). Also y* + r·η(w) = w for w ∈ E′ and x + r·η′(u) = u for u ∈ E (r ≠ 0).
5. (The integrand G is ρ-integrable.) Put G(s, u) := f(Φ(r⁻¹·(s − s₀), η′(u)))·θ(u). G is a.e. strongly measurable for ρ: the first factor is continuous in (s, u), and (s, u) ↦ θ(u) is a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd, step 3). For every (s, u): |G(s, u)| ≤ b(u) := 1_{B̄(x, rR)}(u)·C_f·|θ(u)|. Indeed, if u ∈ B̄(x, rR) use |f| ≤ C_f. If not, ‖η′(u)‖ = r⁻¹·‖u − x‖ > R, so the f-factor vanishes by (*). b is ν-integrable: by integrable_indicator_iff and Measure.restrict_restrict this is integrability of C_f·|θ| on M ∩ B̄(x, rR), which is the hypothesis on θ applied to the compact set K = B̄(x, rR). L¹⌞(0,1) is a finite measure, so (s, u) ↦ b(u) is ρ-integrable (Integrable.comp_snd). Hence G is ρ-integrable (Integrable.mono').
6. (Undoing the blow-up in E′.) Apply blowup_cov with n = m + 1, centre y*, set M̃ and h(z) := f(z)·θ(π(y* + r·z)), then use step 4. This gives LHS = (r^{m+1})⁻¹·∫_{M̃} f(η(w))·θ(π(w)) dH^{m+1}(w).
7. (Transport to ρ.) By product_measure, ∫_{M̃} F dH^{m+1} = ∫ F d(Φ′_*ρ) for F(w) := f(η(w))·θ(π(w)). By MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map (step 1; valid for every integrand), this equals ∫ F(Φ′(p)) dρ(p). By step 4 and π(Φ(s, u)) = u, F(Φ′(s, u)) = f(Φ(r⁻¹·(s − s₀), η′(u)))·θ(u) = G(s, u). Hence LHS = (r^{m+1})⁻¹·∫ G dρ.
8. (Fubini.) By integral_prod (step 5; ν σ-finite), ∫ G dρ = ∫_{(0,1)} H(s) ds, where H(s) := ∫_M G(s, u) dHᵐ(u). Moreover ∫_{(0,1)} H = ∫_{(0,1]} H (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo) = ∫_0^1 H(s) ds (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, 0 ≤ 1).
9. (Substitution.) r·α + s₀ = 0 and r·β + s₀ = 1. intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_add (c = r ≠ 0, d = s₀; no integrability needed) gives ∫_α^β H(r·σ + s₀) dσ = r⁻¹·∫_0^1 H(s) ds.
10. (Slices.) Fix σ. Since r⁻¹·((r·σ + s₀) − s₀) = σ, we get H(r·σ + s₀) = ∫_M f(Φ(σ, η′(u)))·θ(u) dHᵐ(u). By blowup_cov (n = m, centre x, set M, h(w) := f(Φ(σ, w))·θ(x + r·w)) and step 4, a(σ) = (r^m)⁻¹·∫_M f(Φ(σ, η′(u)))·θ(u) dHᵐ(u). Hence H(r·σ + s₀) = r^m·a(σ) for every σ.
11. (Assembly.) α ≤ β because r > 0 and −s₀ ≤ 1 − s₀ (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right). RHS = ∫_{(α,β]} a(σ) dσ (integral_indicator, Ioc measurable) = ∫_α^β a(σ) dσ (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). By steps 9–10 and intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, r^m·∫_α^β a = ∫_α^β H(r·σ + s₀) dσ = r⁻¹·∫_0^1 H. By steps 6–8, LHS = (r^{m+1})⁻¹·∫_0^1 H = (r^m)⁻¹·(r⁻¹·∫_0^1 H) (pow_succ, mul_inv) = (r^m)⁻¹·r^m·∫_α^β a = ∫_α^β a = RHS. ∎
